experiments.scope: Per trial: 256 seeded uniform 256-bit inputs x, messages LE32(x), one batch of the compiled bit-sliced six-round circuit (proof Section 3, Appendix A). Returns two slots whose bit-sliced digests agree on digest bits 0-2 of each of the four digest lanes. A mechanical cross-check, not a full-width equivalence test.
experiments.hypothesis: Every returned pair agrees on the 12 masked digest bits when the organizer recomputes both digests. Reported gate counts are untrusted observations.

experiments.scope: The Section 5 algorithm at reduced width n=14 on the real target: step x <- digest planes 0..13 of LE32(x); 256 slots; DP = digest bit 13 zero; table keyed on bits 0..12; abandonment at 16; reseeding stops after 256 evaluations, then drain; same-batch DPs in slot order; halt at the first RELOCATE (scalar f). One walk per trial.
experiments.hypothesis: Every returned pair is two distinct 32-byte messages whose complete six-round SHA3-256 digests agree on digest bits 0..13 (an absolute 14-bit collision). Failed RELOCATEs and drained walks return null.

experiments.scope: Contact test on the real target at reduced width n=18: N=2^18, exactly K=512 evaluations (2 batches), 256 distinct uniform starts, 256 slots in batch-major slot-minor order. Input window: message bits (7k+11i) mod 256; output window: digest bits {0,12,24,36,48,60,72,84,96,108,120,132,144,156,168,180,192,204} (the six windows are disjoint). A trial returns the first-contact collision pair, or null if the first contact is a start or no contact occurs within K.
experiments.hypothesis: Every returned pair is an absolute 18-bit collision of the real target on the output window. The success frequency is compared descriptively with the random-function prediction for this exact harness (proof Section 10); no iid interval is inferred.
